intro: Length-prefixed frames can carry text containing any delimiter without escaping it. The length counts bytes so a decoder can locate the next frame before interpreting text.
task: Encode and decode UTF-8 text frames with decimal byte lengths and reject malformed frames.
requirements: For mode="encode", value is a sequence of strings: return bytes formed by decimal UTF-8 byte length, colon, then payload for each string, with no separator between frames. Reject encoding if the complete framed stream would exceed 10000000 bytes, including headers. For mode="decode", value is bytes of at most 10000000 bytes: return decoded strings. Length headers must contain 1..8 ASCII digits with no leading zero except "0". Reject missing/truncated frames, invalid UTF-8, or decoded strings over 10000 characters or more than 1000 frames.
Sequence inputs are Python lists or tuples of at most 1000 items. Text inputs contain valid Unicode scalar characters and at most 10000 characters.
Return the documented Python output types and preserve all caller inputs. Raise ValueError for invalid inputs unless the task explicitly reports a record-level rejection.

hints.title: Trace one record
hints.body: Advance by the declared byte length, not by searching for the next colon in a payload.

hints.title: Handle the boundary
hints.body: Decode UTF-8 only after extracting exactly one byte payload.

explanation: Length-prefixed frames can carry text containing any delimiter without escaping it. The length counts bytes so a decoder can locate the next frame before interpreting text.
Strict length syntax removes alternate encodings of the same frame. Truncation and invalid UTF-8 must be reported rather than returning a partial decoded result.
